facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered in July 1996 by William J. de Klerk and Callum Ross during a joint expedition in the Kirkwood Formation.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Nqwebasaurus was discovered from the Kirkwood Formation of the Uitenhage Group by William J. de Klerk of the Albany Museum and Callum Ross of the Stony Brook University in July 1996 during a joint expedition.

facts.statement: The genus name comes from the Xhosa word for the Kirkwood district, and the species name means "fast runner" in ancient Xhosa.
facts.quote: The name Nqwebasaurus is derived from the Xhosa word Nqweba which is the local name for the Kirkwood district, and thwazi is ancient Xhosa for "fast runner".

facts.statement: Nqwebasaurus lived approximately 145 to 140 million years ago during the Berriasian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente 145 a 140 millones de años, durante el Berriasiense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The fossil record indicates Nqwebasaurus lived between 143.1 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (143.1 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Nqwebasaurus represents the oldest known coelurosaur dinosaur found in Africa.
facts.quote: representing the oldest known coelurosaur in Africa

facts.statement: The type specimen stands about 30 cm high and is estimated to be 90 cm long, though the total length is unknown due to incomplete tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The type specimen is approximately 30 cm (1 ft) high and is estimated to have been 90 cm (3 ft) long

facts.statement: It possessed a long, three-fingered hand with a partially opposable thumb featuring a recurved claw.
facts.quote: Nqwebasaurus has a long, three-fingered hand which includes a partially opposable thumb with a recurved claw.

facts.statement: The dinosaur lacked serrations on its upper teeth, had reduced dentition, and contained gastroliths in its abdominal cavity.
facts.quote: Nqwebasaurus also lacks serrations on its maxillary teeth, has a reduced dentition, and contains gastroliths in its abdominal cavity

facts.statement: Based on its morphology, including reduced teeth and gastroliths, it is believed to have been a herbivore.
facts.quote: Debido a estos rasgos morfológicos, Nqwebasaurus, se cree que fue un herbívoro.

facts.statement: It is accepted that Nqwebasaurus likely had at least partial feathers or a feather coat for thermoregulation, similar to basal theropods.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, como las especies de terópodos más basales, especialmente aquellas en la línea evolutiva de las aves, tenían plumas, se acepta que Nqwebasaurus probablemente tenía al menos parcialmente plumas o tenía un abrigo de plumas para la termorregulación.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Nqwebasaurus as the most basal member of the Ornithomimosauria clade.
facts.quote: The most recent phylogenetic analyses that include Nqwebasaurus recovered it in the position as the basalmost member of Ornithomimosauria.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Nqwebasaurus belongs to Ornithomimosauria or represents a basal compsognathid or alvarezsaurid, as older studies suggested different positions.
facts.quote: However, many older studies have recovered different positions for the taxon amongst Coelurosauria, ranging from a basal member of the group, a compsognathid, or an alvarezsaurid.

facts.statement: The name Nqwebasaurus is derived from the Xhosa word Nqweba for the Kirkwood district, and thwazi means "lightning" in ancient Xhosa.
facts.quote: El nombre Nqwebasaurus se deriva de la palabra Xhosa Nqweba, que es el nombre local del distrito de Kirkwood, y thwazi, rayos en xhosa antiguo.
